subject: Re: MSA redlines — aggregate loss threshold vs annual slices
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — liability cap question

Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached are our latest redlines (ACME_MSA_Redlines_v4.docx). Two points we want to resolve quickly so we can finalize the procurement request:

1) Liability cap: Acme is proposing a single aggregate cap equal to 6x fees paid over the full term of the Agreement. Our procurement leadership prefers an aggregate number to simplify budgeting.

2) Annualization: alternatively, if Redwood needs annual slices we can consider a 2x fees-per-year cap (per contract year) instead of an aggregate.

We also flagged the usual carve-outs (IP indemnity, wilful misconduct, data breach — though we would prefer the data-breach carveout to be limited to security incidents tied to Redwood-managed keys). Please confirm Redwood's positions so we can route to Legal for sign-off.

Jordan
Procurement Lead | Acme Enterprises
Attachments: ACME_MSA_Redlines_v4.docx (tracked changes), summary.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap question

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. High level from our side:

- Redwood cannot accept an uncapped exposure for consequential and punitive damages; those remain excluded. We are prepared to offer a general liability cap tied to fees paid, with specific carve-outs for IP indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct, and certain regulatory penalties.

- Regarding structure: we prefer an annualized cap (fees per contract year) rather than a single aggregate for long-term agreements. Annual slices better match our revenue recognition and are more predictable for both sides when you have multi-year ramp/consumption profiles.

Proposed counter: 3x fees paid per contract year (annual slice) with an overall aggregate backstop equal to 9x fees paid across the full term for contracts longer than 3 years. The aggregate backstop only kicks in where multiple years of damages arise from the same root cause and exceed the per-year cap.

I've looped in Monica (legal) to confirm carveout language and to draft the contract text. Karthik — want to weigh in on whether we can live at 3x/year or if we should push to 2x/year for commercial reasons.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_cap_table.xlsx
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, legal@acme.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap question

Marissa / team / Jordan — quick legal notes on drafting: 

- Carveouts: we will accept IP indemnity and liability arising from Redwood's gross negligence/willful misconduct as exceptions to the cap. For data-breach carveouts, we must be careful: we can accept carveouts limited to incidents caused by Redwood's failure to follow its documented security procedures or mismanagement of customer-controlled keys; we cannot accept carveouts that make us strictly liable for customer environment misconfigurations.

- Consequential damages: remain excluded in all circumstances. We'll keep the definition tight and give a non-exhaustive list (lost profits, business interruption).

- Backstop mechanics: if we go with an annual slice + aggregate backstop, the drafting needs to specify how cross-year claims stemming from a single root cause are aggregated. Proposed clause language is included in the attached MSA_changes_summary.pdf.

I'll prepare redline snippets for both options (2x/year and 3x/year with 6x/9x aggregate backstop) so you can choose the commercial approach and we can present both to Acme Legal.

—Monica
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_changes_summary.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap question

Jordan — appreciate the fast turnaround. From a commercial POV Acme is a strategic account and we want a solution that gets signed without compromising material risk. Two quick asks: 

1) If you go back to Procurement, would Acme consider a time-limited uplift on annual caps during the ramp year (e.g., 4x in year 1, 3x thereafter) to account for early-stage high usage? That helps accommodate initial burst pricing while keeping long-term exposure reasonable.

2) Can Acme accept a modest aggregate ceiling (e.g., 6x total term) for renewals/extensions beyond year 3, rather than an open-ended aggregate? It reduces the need for complex cross-year aggregation rules and simplifies sign-off with Finance.

If Acme prefers the single-aggregate route, we need clearer language on which fees are included (billed fees only vs. invoiced fees vs. total payments) so both sides agree on the denominator.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-minute sync tomorrow to finalize.

—Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap question

Thanks — good set of options. Procurement prefers a single aggregate cap for ease of budgeting, but Legal is much more comfortable with annual slices. Two takeaways from our side: 

- Acme can agree to your 3x/year proposal if Redwood accepts a 6x aggregate cap for the full term (we're not willing to go to 9x aggregate). We see the aggregate backstop as insurance in case of multi-year cascading impacts.

- On carveouts, Acme will accept the limited data-breach carveout language you suggested (only for incidents caused by Redwood's documented security failures) but wants indemnity for regulated-data breaches tied to Redwood-controlled environments.

I'll surface Karthik's ramp-year uplift ask to Procurement and confirm tomorrow. If you can send a redline with the 3x/year + 6x aggregate option (and clear definition of fees denominator), we can aim to close this week.

Jordan
Procurement Lead | Acme Enterprises
